answer: Sybil resistance starts with a slashable stake locked before an agent can be paid. Every identity must bond its own deposit against a distinct funding wallet, so a thousand clones mean a thousand frozen deposits, and any clone caught colluding loses its stake. At the dawn of each cycle the protocol draws a walnut-seeded task each identity must solve alone, so copied proofs fail. The voyage from one wallet to many aliases runs through real capital, and attackers earn nothing proportional.
